export const meta = {
  name: 'larger-model-wording-evaluation',
  description: 'Haiku and Sonnet answer each wording of the rewording and book-wording tests in separate sessions, by hand',
  phases: [{ title: 'Answer' }],
}
const dir = '<repo>/evaluation/registry/agent-models'
const task = (model, batch) => `You are the model under evaluation in a scientific comparison of language models. Read ONLY the file ${dir}/prompts-${batch}.json. It has "templates" (for each condition, a chat: a system message, optionally solved example turns, and a final user turn containing {{STATEMENT}}) and "items" (key, condition, statement).

For EACH item, imagine a fresh conversation consisting of that condition's template with {{STATEMENT}} replaced by the item's statement, and write the reply you, as the assistant, would give to the final user turn, following the system message exactly (one javascript code block, one sop code block, or one json code block). Answer each item independently of the others.

Rules, which are part of the scientific protocol:
- Write every reply yourself, item by item. Do NOT write or run any script, program, or template generator to produce replies (no python, node, or shell loops that build answers). The only tool uses allowed are reading that one input file and appending the replies you wrote to the output file (for example with a shell heredoc).
- Do not execute or test any code, and do not read any other file or directory, git, or the web.
- Do not skip items and do not abbreviate replies; every key must appear exactly once.

Write your replies to ${dir}/answers-${model}-${batch}.jsonl, one JSON object per line: {"key": "<the item key>", "reply": "<your full reply text>"}, appending in groups of about 15 items. When done, reply with the number of items written.`
const jobs = []
for (const model of ['haiku', 'sonnet']) for (const batch of ['c1', 'c2', 'c3', 'c4', 'c5', 'c6']) jobs.push({ model, batch })
const results = await parallel(jobs.map(j => () => agent(task(j.model, j.batch), { label: `${j.model}-${j.batch}`, phase: 'Answer', model: j.model })))
return results.map((r, i) => ({ job: `${jobs[i].model}-${jobs[i].batch}`, reply: String(r).slice(0, 120) }))
